title: The Gnome (Dat Erdmänneken)

full_text:
A king had three beautiful daughters who were stolen away into a deep subterranean cavern by an evil enchanter. Three brave huntsman brothers set out to rescue them, scouring the dark forests until they found an ancient castle where a tiny gray gnome dwelled beneath the kitchen flagstones.

The gnome showed them the yawning mouth of an abyss leading deep into the center of the earth. The two older brothers took fright at the dizzying depths and refused to descend. Only the youngest brother, steadfast and courageous, climbed into the wicker basket and was lowered down into the dark chasm.

At the bottom, he fought through enchanted serpents and fire-breathing dragons, rescuing all three princesses and collecting the magnificent golden apples that symbolized their royal heritage. He placed the maidens in the basket one by one and signaled his brothers to haul them up.

When it came time for the youngest brother to be raised, he wisely placed a heavy boulder in the basket instead of himself. As expected, his envious brothers cut the rope halfway up, hoping to kill him and claim the royal brides for themselves.

Trapped in the underworld, the abandoned hero wandered until he found a wounded griffin chick. He fed the young bird and protected it from a ravenous serpent. In gratitude, the mother griffin carried the loyal youth upon her back through the subterranean clouds up into the sunlight.

He presented the princesses with their golden apples, unmasked his treacherous brothers, and took the hand of the youngest princess in a joyous wedding celebrated throughout the land.
moral: True brotherhood is tested in adversity; faithful integrity rises above cowardly treachery.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Gnome (Dat Erdmänneken)"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
